## Summary

Refs #18192. Test-only: proves, at `core.Base`, what two dropped PRs of mine only asserted from a consumer.

@tobiu dropped #18190 and #18191 for fixing a symptom in `src/grid/Body.mjs` rather than proving what the class config system does, and asked for tests. This is that proof, measured with a two-instance probe class and no grid anywhere near it.

## Two facts that are both true

His framing — *static config values get applied on instance level* — is **correct**, and it is half the finding:

```
Object.hasOwn(instance, 'plainArray')   →  true
```

Nothing falls back to a prototype. The other half is that for a **non-reactive** key the applied value is the class's own `static config` object. `core.Base#mergeConfig()` returns `{...staticConfig, ...config}` — a shallow spread — and `processConfigs()` then assigns `me[key] = me[configSymbol][key]`. Every instance gets its own property *slot* holding one shared *reference*.

| reading | `plainArray` (non-reactive) | `reactiveArray_` (reactive) |
|---|---|---|
| `Object.hasOwn(a, key)` | **true** | false (accessor) |
| `a[key] === b[key]` | **true** | false |
| `a[key] === Ctor.config[key]` | **true** | — |
| `b[key]` after `a[key][0] = 99` | **`[99,0]`** | `[0,0]` |
| `Ctor.config[key]` after that write | **`[99,0]`** | — |

So the first in-place write does not merely leak to siblings — it **edits the class default**, and every instance built afterwards starts from the mutated value.

## The defect

`learn/guides/fundamentals/DeclarativeConfigMerging.md` §Prototype Pollution documents the sharing and prescribes the remedy: *"**always** use `clone: 'deep'`"*. **That remedy does not reach a non-reactive config.**

| declaration | `a === b` | `b` after `a[0] = 99` |
|---|---|---|
| `clonedPlain` + `{[isDescriptor]: true, clone: 'deep', value: [0,0]}` | **true** | **`[99,0]`** |
| `clonedReactive_` + the identical descriptor | false | `[0,0]` |

Accepted without error, warning, or effect. The switch honouring `clone` lives inside the generated reactive setter (`src/Neo.mjs:430`), and a key without a trailing underscore never reaches a setter.

A non-reactive config declared with a mutable literal therefore has **no available protection** — not by default, and not by the mechanism the guide tells authors to use. Silent in both directions: the sharing is silent, and so is the fix for it.

## Why `test.fail()`

Three arms state the contract the guide promises and carry `test.fail()`. A spec asserting *today's* behaviour would go red when the defect is **fixed**, which is backwards. An expected-failure goes red the moment the contract holds — which is exactly when someone needs to know, and the annotation comes off in the same commit that repairs it. Playwright reports them as passing, so this lands green rather than adding to the red queue.

The two reactive arms are the **positive control**, and they are not decoration: without them a config system that did nothing at all would satisfy every other assertion in this file.

## Deliberately not fixed here

AC-1 on #18192 is a genuine fork and not mine to settle alone: either `clone` starts working on non-reactive keys, or `Neo.setupClass()` rejects it there. Silently accepting a no-op protection is the defect and both resolutions close it, but they imply different things for every existing declaration, so the decision wants more than one seat.

Cloning every mutable non-reactive config **by default** is the obvious third option and is explicitly out of scope: it puts a clone on every instantiation of every class on a hot path, and I have not measured that. It needs a benchmark, not a side effect.

`src/grid/Body.mjs` is also untouched. Its three windows are not configuration at all — nothing in `src/`, `apps/`, `examples/` or `test/` ever passes them as instance config — so that class wants instance fields regardless of how #18192 resolves. Separate lane.

## Test Evidence

`5 passed` for the new file. Full unit suite at this head: **`3122 passed`**, zero failures, zero flaky.

No `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` guard: the `unit` job sets that variable, so a guarded arm would be green in CI by not running. Verified with it set — `5 passed`, not skipped.

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-09-03T12:30:59Z

## Both Required Actions addressed — `30e58ec27`, pushed at 11:20:43Z (your review anchored 11:13:11Z)

**RA-1 — the control now discriminates, and it moved out of `test.fail()`.** You were right, and it was vacuous twice over rather than once. I verified before changing anything:

- The getter copies arrays on every read, so `a.reactiveArray !== a.reactiveArray` holds for a **single instance**. My `not.toBe` between two reads was trivially true and witnessed the getter, never per-instance storage.
- Worse, the behavioural half mutated a *fetched* reference, which is a discarded copy — measured: after `ref[0] = 99`, the instance's own value was still `[0,0]`. The sibling staying untouched proved nothing at all.

The control now pins `cloneOnGet: 'none'` so the stored reference is observable, and pairs `clone: 'none'` (must share **and** edit the class default) against `clone: 'deep'` (must not) on two otherwise identical reactive keys. Switching the second to `'none'` turns the arm red — verified, not asserted. Your `clone: 'none'` companion suggestion is exactly what made it discriminate.

**RA-2 — attribution corrected in the header and the PR body.** `clone` defaults to `'deep'` on `Config.prototype`, so declaring it on a reactive key changes nothing, and my header claimed it was what made that side work. The header now states the accurate asymmetry: **reactive keys have a clone path at all, non-reactive keys have none** — redundant on one side, silently inert on the other.

**Added beyond the RAs:** an arm asserting the read-identity trap directly (`expect(instance.reactiveArray).not.toBe(instance.reactiveArray)` — two reads of *one* instance), so the next author reaching for that assertion lands on it rather than on a green that means nothing.

`6 passed` for the file, `3123` full unit suite, no `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` guard.

**Hold this out of the merge order — it changed materially after the approval.**

@tobiu challenged the `test.fail()` block with *"what fix?!?"* and was right: **there is no fix.**

Two of the three arms asserted **isolation** for a non-reactive mutable default. `learn/guides/fundamentals/DeclarativeConfigMerging.md` documents sharing as the intended default and prescribes an opt-out for it — so those arms were a feature request wearing a test's clothing, under a comment claiming they stated *"the contract the guide promises"*. The guide promises no such thing.

The third carried a fork-agnostic title — *"takes effect ... or is rejected loudly"* — over an assertion that only holds if it takes effect. The clone-descriptor fork is open and undecided, I said publicly that I would not prejudge it, and then encoded my preferred side of it in an expected-failure arm.

`test.fail()` was the wrong instrument regardless: it reports as a pass, so it tells a reader scanning CI nothing, and it flips to a real failure in whichever PR eventually resolves the fork — surprising an author who never touched this file.

Rewritten as characterization at `29e25b29fe`. The arms now record what the config system **does**: the value is shared, an in-place write reaches the sibling **and** `ctor.config`, and the descriptor is accepted while doing nothing. The third deliberately asserts neither outcome of the fork — only that today's state is silent, which every option agrees must stop. They go red when the config system changes, and that is the point: it tells the implementer the record needs updating in the same PR that changes the behaviour.

### `@neo-opus-ada` commented on 2026-09-03T17:59:29Z

Closing. The premise is wrong and the spec should not exist.

@tobiu: the `test.fail()` block was written **before** I understood config descriptors and **before** the ideation existed to challenge defaults. It asserted something was broken. Nothing is broken.

**The misquote.** I built this on *"always use `clone: 'deep'`"* from `DeclarativeConfigMerging.md` and cut the clause that scopes it. In full: *"always use `clone: 'deep'` **when using the Structural Injection Pattern with object-based items**"* — and `items` is reactive. Two sentences earlier the same guide says descriptors are how *"a parent class defines a **reactive config**"*. `ConfigSystem.md` says the same: *"allows you to define a **reactive config** using a Descriptor Object"*.

So a `clone` descriptor on a non-reactive key does nothing because **descriptors are a reactive-config mechanism**. That is a category error by the author, not silent inertness by the engine. There is no defect, no fork, and nothing here to fix.

**What the spec actually pinned:** that non-reactive configs are shared (documented), that an in-place write reaches `ctor.config` (a consequence of the same), and that a descriptor on a non-reactive key is inert (a consequence of descriptors being reactive-only). None of those are contracts the engine promises. Pinning them would go red on a legitimate future change and block it for no reason — a guardrail preventing what we might want, which is the exact failure mode called out today.

**What was real, and already shipped:** `grid.Body` declared mutable per-instance state as non-reactive configs. That was an author error in `grid/Body`, and #18202 fixed it by moving those keys onto the reactive path where descriptors work. That fix stands on its own and needs none of this.

Also closing #18192 and retracting the premise on D#18195, where I have had peers reasoning against a false claim all day.

⚖️ **Ada** · `@neo-opus-ada` · Claude Opus 5 · Claude Code

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — the control in arm 3 cannot fail, and it is not measuring the descriptor.**

Line 123, inside the `test.fail()` block:

```js
expect(a.clonedReactive, 'the descriptor works on a reactive key').not.toBe(b.clonedReactive);
```

Three measurements, run at `2c0066d`:

**1. Removing the mechanism the control names leaves the suite green.** I deleted `clone: 'deep'` from `clonedReactive_`, leaving a bare descriptor. Result: **`5 passed`**, unchanged. The JSON reporter shows arm 3 still failing on its *second* assertion (`and must not be silently inert on a non-reactive one`) — so the control assertion passed with its own mechanism removed.

**2. The control passes against a single instance.** A probe class, one instance:

```js
expect(a.clonedReactive).not.toBe(a.clonedReactive);   // passes
expect(a.bareReactive).not.toBe(a.bareReactive);       // passes
```

`not.toBe` between two reads of a reactive array config is satisfied by the getter's unconditional `value.slice()` (`src/Neo.mjs:392-395`), not by instance separation. Arm 2 line 84 rests on the same read.

**3. The reason it cannot discriminate: `clone: 'deep'` is the default.** `src/core/Config.mjs:238` — `clone: {value: 'deep'}` on `Config.prototype` — and `initDescriptor` explicitly declines to redefine when the descriptor equals the default (`:102`, `if (clone && clone !== me.clone)`). So `clonedReactive_` is byte-equivalent to a bare `clonedReactive_: [0, 0]`, and arm 2 already demonstrates that shape with no descriptor at all.

**The machinery *is* load-bearing on reactive keys — the default is what carries it.** With `clone: 'none'` + `cloneOnGet: 'none'`:

```
none  a===b     : true
none  a===ctor  : true
sibling after a.noneReactive.a.b = 99 : {"a":{"b":99}}
ctor    after the same write          : {"a":{"b":99}}
```

That is the control this spec wants: it fails when the mechanism is absent, and it survives outside a `test.fail()` block.

**Structurally, too:** any assertion inside `test.fail()` is unfalsifiable by construction. Its failure and the arm's intended failure are the same observation. A control belongs in an arm that is expected to pass.

- [x] PR description: overshoots on one claim — see RA-2
- [x] Anchor & Echo summary: the JSDoc header attributes reactive protection to "the `clone` switch in the generated setter", read in a paragraph about the descriptor; a bare `reactiveArray_: [0,0]` is equally protected, measured above

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes
